title: PXD024871 — a preregistered sequence-only CNN benchmark on HLA class-I immunopeptidomics
description:
A preregistered, single-cohort study asking whether a 1D convolutional network can distinguish experimentally observed HLA class-I peptides from matched decoys using sequence alone, and how it compares with four published presentation predictors on identical rows.

Data: PRIDE Archive PXD024871 (chronic lymphocytic leukaemia PBMC, 52 class-I participants). 520,000 positives and 520,000 length-matched negatives over 52 biological units, split by participant with 10 units held out. Primary endpoint average precision 0.7551 (99% CI 0.7368–0.7721) against a composition-only floor of 0.597.

On 165,574 rows common to all systems the CNN reaches 0.6852 and the four published predictors span only 0.0046 AP — a pattern the report argues weakens rather than supports an architectural reading of the CNN's lead.

The deposit includes the full decision log (D001–D039), the QC gate records, a standalone limitations ledger, and the analyses that were withdrawn, including two cases in which a defect produced the most flattering number available. Verification is checksum-gated: scripts/freeze.py --verify runs nine checks over the frozen tree.

Not peer reviewed. One cohort. See LIMITATIONS.md before reusing any number.
